claim: Individuals who were neither parties nor privies to consent decrees are not precluded from bringing independent Title VII discrimination claims based on actions taken pursuant to those decrees, but a consent decree entered pursuant to voluntary settlement provides greater protection against charges of illegal discrimination than a voluntary affirmative action plan due to its formal judicial endorsement.
initial_reasoning: The cited case (833 F.2d 1492) holds that individuals who were neither parties nor privies to the consent decrees are not precluded from bringing independent Title VII claims, but it also rejects the notion that a consent decree entered pursuant to a voluntary settlement affords greater protection than a voluntary affirmative‑action plan. Thus the citation does not support the claim that such decrees provide superior protection.
